name_of_eltif.label: Name of ELTIF
name_of_eltif.help: The official name of the fund under which it will be offered to investors.

legal_form.label: Legal Form
legal_form.help: The legal "wrapper" of the fund. A SICAV is a variable-capital company issuing investment shares; an open-ended mutual fund has no legal personality — it is run by a management company and issues units. The choice affects who manages the fund and what securities you hold.

self_managed.label: Self-Managed
self_managed.help: Whether the SICAV manages its own assets (holds its own licence) or delegates management to an external company. Not applicable to a mutual fund.

name_of_aifm.label: AIFM
name_of_aifm.help: The licensed company that actually runs the fund — decides on investments and ensures the rules are followed.

name_of_management_company.label: Management Company
name_of_management_company.help: The management company that created and runs the mutual fund. A mutual fund is not a company itself, so it is always run by this company.

name_of_investment_manager.label: Investment Manager
name_of_investment_manager.help: Who actually selects the specific investments, where this role is delegated. Optional.

name_of_administrator.label: Administrator
name_of_administrator.help: The company providing the fund's operational back office — accounting, valuation, reporting.

name_of_depositary.label: Depositary
name_of_depositary.help: The bank or broker that safekeeps the fund's assets and oversees their movements. Required by law for every fund.

fund_reference_currency.label: Reference Currency
fund_reference_currency.help: The base currency in which the fund's total value is calculated. Holdings in other currencies are converted into it.

duration.label: Duration ('end of life')
duration.help: How long the fund operates — either with no fixed end, or until a set date after which the fund is wound up and its assets sold.

duration_limited_to.label: Duration — Limited To
duration_limited_to.help: The number of years after which the fund ends.

strategy_ioas.label: Investment Objective and Strategy
strategy_ioas.help: A description of what the fund invests in, why, and what it aims to achieve.

strategy_tatuea.label: Target Allocation to UCITS Eligible Assets
strategy_tatuea.help: The maximum share held in ordinary, easily sellable securities (shares, bonds); the rest goes into long-term investments — the essence of an ELTIF. Note: 45% is a ceiling arising from the ELTIF requirement to hold at least 55% in long-term eligible assets and cannot be set higher.

strategy_ilseeia.label: Investment Limitation in a Single ELTIF Eligible Asset
strategy_ilseeia.help: The maximum share of the fund in a single long-term investment — prevents over-reliance on one project. Note: because the fund is retail, 20% is a legal cap under ELTIF diversification rules (Art. 13) and cannot be set higher.

strategy_ilsuea.label: Investment Limitation in a Single UCITS Eligible Asset
strategy_ilsuea.help: The maximum share of the fund in a single ordinary security. Note: for a retail fund, 10% is a legal cap (Art. 13 ELTIF).

strategy_apac.label: Additional Portfolio Allocation Considerations
strategy_apac.help: Space for additional rules on portfolio allocation.

strategy_ramp_up_period.label: Ramp-Up Period
strategy_ramp_up_period.help: How long after launch it takes for the fund to fully invest the money it has raised.

sfdr_category.label: SFDR Article
sfdr_category.help: The fund's sustainability level under EU rules: Article 6 = no specific focus, Article 8 = considers environmental/social factors, Article 9 = directly targets sustainable impact.

target_investors.label: Target Investors
target_investors.help: Who the fund is for. This fund is aimed solely at retail investors, who receive stronger protection and a lower permitted level of fund borrowing. The value is fixed.

leverage_borrowing_amount.label: Borrowing — Amount
leverage_borrowing_amount.help: How much the fund may borrow on top of investors' money, as a % of fund value. Borrowing can increase both return and loss. Note: for a retail fund the legal cap is 50% of NAV.

leverage_borrowing_maturity.label: Borrowing — Maturity
leverage_borrowing_maturity.help: For how long the fund borrows.

leverage_aifmd_commitment_method.label: AIFMD Leverage — Commitment Method
leverage_aifmd_commitment_method.help: The fund's leverage measured by one of the officially prescribed methods (includes derivatives). Used to compare risk across funds.

leverage_aifmd_gross_method.label: AIFMD Leverage — Gross Method
leverage_aifmd_gross_method.help: The second officially prescribed leverage calculation, "gross", without netting offsetting positions.

share_class.label: Share Class
share_class.help: A variant of the same fund. An accumulation class keeps and reinvests returns; a distribution class pays them out to you regularly.

currency.label: Currency
currency.help: The currency in which this class is denominated.

minimum_subscription_amount.label: Minimum Subscription Amount
minimum_subscription_amount.help: The lowest amount that can be invested into this class at once.

management_fee.label: Management Fee
management_fee.help: The annual fund management fee, as a % of the investment.

performance_fee.label: Performance Fee
performance_fee.help: The manager's reward from above-benchmark profit. "Hurdle" = the minimum return the fund must beat; "high water mark" = the fee is charged only on new highs, not repeatedly on the same profit.
performance_fee.placeholder: XX %, subject to XX % hurdle & high water mark…

distribution_frequency.label: Distribution Frequency
distribution_frequency.help: How often a distribution class pays returns to you. Complete only for distribution classes.

subscription_fee.label: Subscription Fee
subscription_fee.help: A one-off fee when buying units, as a % of the amount invested.

redemption_fee.label: Redemption Fee
redemption_fee.help: A fee when leaving the fund. Besides income, it protects remaining investors from the costs triggered by others exiting (anti-dilution).

anti_dilution_lmt.label: Anti-Dilution LMT
anti_dilution_lmt.help: Tools ensuring the costs of some investors leaving are borne by those leaving, not those staying. The law does not require them but recommends at least one.

subscription_frequency.label: Subscription Frequency
subscription_frequency.help: When investors can enter the fund (e.g. the first day of each month).

subscription_cut_off_time.label: Subscription Cut-Off Time
subscription_cut_off_time.help: How many days before the subscription date a request to enter must be received.

subscription_payment_date.label: Subscription Payment Date
subscription_payment_date.help: How many days before the subscription date the investor must send the money.

nav_calculation_date.label: NAV Calculation Date
nav_calculation_date.help: The date on which the value of a unit (NAV) is set, at which units are bought and sold.

redemption_calibration_method.label: Redemption Calibration Method
redemption_calibration_method.help: The law offers two ways to calculate how much the fund may pay out to exiting investors on a single payout day. Annex I derives the cap from how often redemptions can be requested and how far in advance you must give notice — longer notice allows a larger share to be paid. Annex II instead requires the fund to hold a permanent buffer of easily sellable assets and sets the cap from its size. Choose one.

redemption_frequency.label: Redemption Frequency
redemption_frequency.help: How often during the year you can request your money back. More frequent redemptions mean stricter conditions, because the fund holds long-term investments that cannot be sold quickly.

redemption_notice_period.label: Redemption Notice Period
redemption_notice_period.help: How far in advance you must announce you want your money back before the fund pays out. Longer notice gives the fund time to sell assets and so allows a larger share to be paid at once.

min_liquid_assets_pct.label: Minimum Liquid Assets
min_liquid_assets_pct.help: What share of the fund must be permanently held in cash and easily sellable assets, so there is something to pay out from. The more frequent the redemptions, the larger the buffer the law requires.

max_redemption_pct.label: Maximum Redemption %
max_redemption_pct.help: The highest share of the fund's available money that can be paid out on a single payout day. Calculated automatically from your choice of method, frequency and notice.

liquid_assets_amount.label: Liquid Assets
liquid_assets_amount.help: The value of the fund's easily sellable assets (cash, ordinary securities) from which payouts can be met.

expected_cashflow_12m.label: Expected 12m Cash Flow
expected_cashflow_12m.help: Money the fund is highly certain to receive over the coming year (e.g. repayments, income). Money from new investors is not counted.

redemption_cut_off.label: Redemption Cut-Off Time
redemption_cut_off.help: How many days before the payout day a redemption request must be received.

redemption_dealing_date.label: Redemption Date
redemption_dealing_date.help: The day on which redemptions are processed.

payment_of_redemption_proceeds.label: Payment of Redemption Proceeds
payment_of_redemption_proceeds.help: How many days after the payout day the investor receives the money.

carry_policy.label: Treatment of Unexecuted Requests
carry_policy.help: When more people request a redemption on one day than the fund may pay, requests are scaled down proportionally. Here you set what happens to the remainder: it automatically moves to the next payout day in the queue, or it lapses and the investor must request again, or the choice is left to the investor.

min_holding_period.label: Minimum Holding Period
min_holding_period.help: The shortest period an investor must hold units before first requesting a redemption.

redemption_in_kind.label: Repayment in Kind
redemption_in_kind.help: Whether the fund may pay an exiting investor directly with a portion of its assets instead of cash.

redemptions_simulation.label: Redemptions Simulation
redemptions_simulation.help: An interactive demonstration: based on the fund's settings, it calculates when and how much an exiting investor would actually receive — including when many people want to exit at once.

asset_class.label: Asset Class
asset_class.help: Which category the investment belongs to. The first seven are the ELTIF long-term "eligible" assets; the last is the liquid reserve.

asset_class_amount.label: Asset Class Amount
asset_class_amount.help: How much is invested in this category.

eltif_capital.label: ELTIF Capital
eltif_capital.help: The fund's investable capital (contributions plus uncalled commitments, net of fees) — the regulatory base against which investment limits are measured.

nav.label: Net Asset Value
nav.help: The fund's net value after deducting liabilities.

total_assets.label: Total Investment
total_assets.help: The total amount invested (sum of the categories).

total_eligible_pct.label: Eligible Assets %
total_eligible_pct.help: The share of long-term eligible assets in capital; at least 55% by law.

avg_liquidity.label: Average Liquidity
avg_liquidity.help: Indicative annual liquidity: how much of the fund's accessible portion can be redeemed per year, plus the number of redemption windows per year.

title.label: Title
title.help: Salutation of the contact person (Ms / Mr).

email.label: Email
email.help: The email to which the generated term sheet will be sent.

agreement.label: Consent
agreement.help: I am aware that Finreg processes my personal data for the purpose of responding to my request.
agreement.checkboxLabel: I am aware that Finreg processes my personal data for the purpose of responding to my request
